issue.title: plugins: a provider whose models are spoken to with @ai-sdk/google can't be tested (Test models off, provider test refuses CodeAssist)
issue.body:
## What happens A plugin provider whose models are spoken to with `@ai-sdk/google` has **Test models disabled in the GUI** ("{name} is reached through its own API… Ask the model from an agent to try it"), and **Test this model** on a model's right-click is off for the same reason. `magpie provider test ` refuses with `this provider can't be sent a test request`. This is the Google Vertex AI case: a plugin that signs in with a user's gcloud / ADC credentials and sends Gemini's own `generateContent` requests to `…/publishers/google` — the same protocol magpie's built-in `google-vertex` preset speaks. The inference itself works; only the probe is refused. Installed magpie: 0.1.1336. `internal/provider/test.go`, `plugins.go`, `provider.go` and `translated_probe.go` are byte-identical between v0.1.1336, v0.1.1343 and `main`, so this is current. ## Why `pluginProtocol` maps the AI SDK package to a protocol (`internal/provider/plugins.go:136-150`): ```go case "@ai-sdk/google": return CodeAssist ``` `pluginProviderServing` then has an address for Chat, Responses, Anthropic and CodeAssist — but **not** `p.Gemini` (`plugins.go:434-445`): ```go case CodeAssist: a.codeAssist = pluginBase + pp.ID ``` So `Speaks()` yields `[CodeAssist]` for such a plugin (`provider.go:1462-1465`), and the two gates that decide whether a probe can be sent both exclude CodeAssist: - `ModelTest()` (`test.go:144-160`) — returns `""` only for Chat, Responses, Anthropic, or `Gemini` with a base. CodeAssist falls through to `"own-api"`, which is what greys the button. - `testOne()` (`test.go:259, 289-297`) — keeps `Chat | Responses | Anthropic | Gemini` and refuses with `this provider can't be sent a test request` when nothing is left. `testsTranslated()` doesn't cover this either: it is deliberately `!p.IsPlugin()` (`translated_probe.go:29-31`), because a plugin's fetch *is* the endpoint — there is a real request to send, unlike a Google sign-in reached through an agent's API. The rest of the path already exists. `pluginFetch` understands a Code Assist envelope and turns it into the publisher URL (`plugins.go:517-528`, `555-556`): ```go case codeAssist: url = base + "/models/" + api + ":streamGenerateContent?alt=sse" ``` which for a plugin whose loader gives `…/v1beta1/projects/

/locations//publishers/google` is exactly the Vertex route. ## Evidence `magpie provider test` (provider level) *does* try CodeAssist, because `Test()` just loops `Speaks()` (`test.go:66`) — it never consults `ModelTest()`: ``` $ magpie provider test gcp-ai ✗ codeassist Refusing to send a Vertex credential outside the configured Google model endpoint ``` That failure is `tinyBody()`'s, not the vendor's: there is no `case CodeAssist` (`test.go:183-205`), so it returns `"", ""`, `pluginFetch` sees an empty rest and resolves the URL to the loader's base itself, and the plugin's own fetch guard refuses it. So the GUI and the CLI disagree, and both are one small branch away from working. ``` $ magpie provider test gcp-ai gemini-2.5-flash ✗ gemini-2.5-flash · this provider can't be sent a test request ``` ## Suggested fix Three spots, all in `internal/provider/test.go`: 1. `ModelTest()` — a plugin with a CodeAssist address can be probed: ```go if p.IsPlugin() && p.Account != nil && p.Account.codeAssist != "" { return "" } ``` 2. `testOne()` — let CodeAssist into the candidate list for a plugin: ```go if pr == Chat || pr == Responses || pr == Anthropic || pr == Gemini || pr == CodeAssist && p.IsPlugin() { ``` 3. `tinyBody()` — the envelope `pluginFetch` already unwraps: ```go case CodeAssist: return q.Base(CodeAssist) + "/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse", fmt.Sprintf(`{"model":%q,"request":{"contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"hi"}]}],"generationConfig":{"maxOutputTokens":16}}}`, model) ``` One detail: `tiny()` appends `,"stream":true}` when `q.Account.Stream` (`test.go:97-101`), and a plugin account always has `Stream: true` (`plugins.go:382`). On the envelope that adds a top-level `"stream"` field, which `pluginFetch`'s struct ignores — harmless, but it means the inner `request` carries no stream field, while the URL `pluginFetch` builds is always `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`. Worth a thought if the probe is to mirror a real request exactly. ## What does not work as a workaround Naming the plugin's provider `google-vertex` (or reusing the preset id) doesn't help. `IsVertex()` is `p.Preset == VertexPreset` (`vertex.go:75`) — a `Preset` field, not the id — and a plugin provider is built as `Provider{ID: id, Name: name, Icon: …, Account: a}` with no preset (`plugins.go:422`); `plugin.Provider` (`internal/plugin/providers.go:115-152`) has no `preset` field at all, so a plugin has no way to say it is Vertex. The id would also be rewritten to `google-vertex-plugin` by `PluginID()` (`plugins.go:51-59`) and every saved sign-in keyed by the provider id would be lost. On the plugin side there is nothing to change: `@ai-sdk/google` is the correct package for Vertex's native protocol, and swapping it for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` to get a testable Chat base would mean giving up the Gemini protocol (thought signatures across tool turns, Vertex's own usage and caching numbers). Thanks — the rest of the plugin path (`loader` base, `pluginFetch`, model listing) works well with a Vertex publisher base; it's only the probe that can't reach it.

comments.body:
The refusal is in the probe, not in inference: `pluginProtocol` maps a plugin model's `@ai-sdk/google` to CodeAssist (`internal/provider/plugins.go`), and `pluginProviderServing` has no address for that protocol, so `ModelTest` answers "own-api" (Test models off, "Ask the model from an agent to try it") and `testOne` returns "this provider can't be sent a test request" — even though the plugin's `fetch` speaks Code Assist fine.

Fixed on [fix/plugin-codeassist-probe](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/plugin-codeassist-probe) (`d99b2bd1`, based on today's `main` `01468003`): a plugin's Code Assist address is a probe target in `ModelTest` and `testOne` (internal/provider/test.go), and `tinyBody` builds the `{"model":…,"request":{…}}` envelope `pluginFetch` already unwraps into the publisher's `streamGenerateContent` — the same shape a Google sign-in's requests are built with. A Google sign-in that is not a plugin keeps its translator path unchanged.

- RED → GREEN: `TestPluginGoogleModelIsTestable` drives the GUI's own gate and the CLI probe; on `01468003` with only the test added it fails with your symptoms — `the GUI's Test models is off: "own-api"` and `fake-gemini tested: … Error:this provider can't be sent a test request` — and `TestPluginTestProbesCodeAssist` shows no probe reaching the publisher (`["/v1?\n"]`). At the head both pass and the publisher receives `/v1/models/fake-gemini:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`.
- `internal/provider` (`-tags nogui`) passes these; `gofmt -l` clean; `go vet`/`go build` clean on linux, windows and `-tags nogui linux`. `docs/subsystems/providers-accounts.md` states the rule in the same commit.
- Not tried, plainly: a real Vertex publisher and the community plugin's own fetch guard end to end — the test uses magpie's fake plugin (`fake-gemini` on `@ai-sdk/google`), so what is proven is that the probe is built and sent through the plugin path rather than refused before it.
